title: Search Typeahead Suggestions
summary: Return ranked query completions with every keystroke while adapting to trending searches.
statement:
Design the autocomplete service for a global search box that suggests the top query completions as a user types each character.

Functional requirements:
- Given a typed prefix, return up to 10 ranked query completions ordered by popularity and recency.
- Update suggestions continuously enough that breaking news or trending topics appear within 15 to 30 minutes.
- Filter out offensive, sensitive, or policy-violating phrases immediately when flagged.

Scale to assume:
- 500 million daily active searchers.
- Peak prefix traffic of 1.5 million requests per second.
- End-to-end server latency under 30 ms at the 99th percentile.
hints: Walking an entire subtree of millions of completions on every keystroke is too slow. What can you precompute and store directly at each prefix?
Updating a shared trie on every single user search creates massive write contention. Separate the read path from the pipeline that builds and refreshes the index.
How do you reduce request volume from fast typists on the client, and how do you remove a newly banned phrase in seconds without waiting for a full index rebuild?
expectations: Clarifies language/locale scoping, personalization versus global suggestions, maximum prefix length, and freshness targets.
Estimates keystroke QPS from daily searchers and average query length, noting how client debouncing and browser prefix caching cut server load.

Serves reads from an in-memory prefix structure (compressed trie with top-K completions cached on each node, or a flat prefix-to-top-K key-value table) sharded by prefix range and replicated per region.
Never mutates the serving trie on live search traffic; instead samples search logs into an aggregation pipeline that applies time-decay weighting and publishes periodic snapshots.
Applies a fast, dynamically pushed blocklist filter in the serving tier so flagged phrases disappear within seconds between index snapshots.
Addresses hot short prefixes (`a`, `th`, `we`) via CDN/edge caching and local gateway caches.
Discusses prefix normalization (case folding, whitespace, diacritics) and basic typo tolerance or locale partitioning.
